av_event.line_text: I know how that feels, mate, honestly. First year I was off I felt proper useless. You get used to it. Not saying it's right, but you do. What you looking at doing, then, anything?
av_event.what: Mark's grin drops and he looks down and away from the camera for a few seconds, rubbing his stubble, before looking back at the screen and carrying on.

text:
B: Hiya mate, can you hear me alright? Mark, from Brierley Hill, near Dudley.
A: Yeah, er, I can hear you. I'm Craig. Lowestoft.
B: Lowestoft! Right on the coast, ain't it? Never been. Furthest east I've got is Great Yarmouth on a works do, and I don't remember much of that, to be honest with you.
A: Ha. Yeah, it's just down the road from Yarmouth. Bit quieter.
B: Did you do that puzzle thing at the start? I was sat there going round in circles, I'll be honest. Julie come in and asked if I was alright 'cause I was swearing at the laptop.
A: Erm, yeah. I dunno how I did. Sort of just guessed the last few.
B: Same, mate, same. So what do you do with yourself, then?
A: Er... nothing at the minute really. I was a welder, fabricator, at an offshore yard. Got laid off last year, then my back went, so.
B: Oh, your back, yeah? Join the club. Mine's been knackered three years now. I was on a depot near Merry Hill, picking and loading, and one day it just went, and the knee went with it. Body's done what it can, ain't it. Doctor says to me, Mark, you've got the spine of a seventy year old, and I says, well give it me back then, 'cause I want the one I had! Nah, I'm alright, I get by. Do bits for mates when I can.
A: Yeah. Mine's the lower back. Physio give me stretches. I do 'em when I remember.
B: When you remember, yeah, that's the trick, ain't it. I've got a sheet of 'em stuck on the fridge, Julie points at it every morning.
A: Ha. Yeah. Gemma's the same. My wife. She's a care assistant, works nights a lot.
B: No! Julie's in care an' all. Part-time though. Hard work, that. They don't get paid what they should.
A: No, they don't. She's sort of carrying everything at the minute, so. Yeah.
B: I know how that feels, mate, honestly. First year I was off I felt proper useless. You get used to it. Not saying it's right, but you do. What you looking at doing, then, anything?
A: Erm, maybe maintenance, workshop stuff. Or forklift. Something lighter. I dunno really.
B: Forklift! I had me licence, let it lapse. Wanna keep yours up, whatever you do, I'm telling you.
A: Yeah, my welding tickets have gone and lapsed an' all. Never was good at keeping on top of that side of it.
B: Nobody is, mate. Paperwork. Who's got time for it. You got a dog? I can see a mug there, is that Ipswich?
A: Yeah, Ipswich. And yeah, Staffy. Dexter. Bit on the chunky side.
B: Staffy! I've got a Staffie cross, Roxy. She's down there somewhere snoring. Chunky's alright, they're built like that, ain't they, little barrels.
A: Ha, that's him. He's got a dodgy stomach as well, so he's a nightmare if he gets hold of anything. Ate half a sausage roll off the seafront last week, I was up at three with him.
B: Oh no. Oh, I've been there. Roxy had a whole bap off my grandson once, ham and all, and the next morning, well, I won't describe it, you might be having your tea. So Ipswich, eh? How they doing?
A: Alright, actually. Better than they have been. Been to Portman Road a couple times with my brother-in-law.
B: I'm Albion, West Brom, had a season ticket for years. Watch it down the pub now with my lad. It's the moaning I miss, you know, sat with all the same blokes moaning every week.
A: Yeah. I watch it on my phone mostly. Bit quiet on your own.
B: You wanna get down the pub for it, mate, even with a lemonade. Gets you out the house. That's what saved me, the darts on a Thursday.
A: Yeah... fair enough. I've got a motorbike in the yard I'm meant to be doing up, that's sort of my thing.
B: You're joking! I've got an old Escort in the garage, been nearly done since about two thousand and nine.
A: Ha. Mine's two years. A 125. Watch loads of them restoration videos on YouTube, then go out there and just look at it.
B: That's it, that's exactly it, you look at it, you have a cup of tea, you go back in. We should start a club, mate.
A: Yeah. Yeah, it's alright, that.
